name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district with incumbent Jill Tokuda running for a second term
Tokuda's lopsided money edge: $570K on hand versus $16K for Awa, plus outside support on her side
No public polls or expert ratings; fundamentals carry the forecast
Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 95%, a touch below pure fundamentals
model.rationale: A Democratic-leaning district, an entrenched incumbent, and a cash advantage of more than thirty to one leave Brenton Awa without a visible path; prediction markets and the fundamentals both point to a comfortable Tokuda re-election.
model.watch: Any polling putting Awa within single digits, or a late surge of outside spending against Tokuda, would be the first sign of a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jill Tokuda seeks a second term representing a Hawaii district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. She holds a decisive financial edge, with roughly $570,000 in the bank compared with $16,000 for Republican Brenton Awa, and the outside spending reported so far supports her candidacy. No public general-election polls have been released, and no national race raters have weighed in on the contest.

Everything that can be measured points the same direction: the district's partisan lean, an incumbency advantage, a wide fundraising gap, and prediction markets pricing Tokuda's win probability around 95 percent. Awa has raised modest sums and attracted no reported outside backing, leaving little evident way to close a fundamentals-based gap in the low twenties. Absent unexpected developments, the seat appears firmly in Democratic hands.
